name: Aguinaldo Shrine
fee_operational_notes: Free entry; voluntary donations welcome.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: NHCP lists 8:00-16:00; several current map listings say 9:00-16:00.

name: Anawangin Cove
fee_operational_notes: ₱100 standard day pass; overnight camping is ₱150.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional water/activity rental; optional camping/tent/campsite fee
hours_note: An ungated campsite reached by boat from Pundaquit, so there is no posted closing time. Boats run on demand rather than to a timetable, and quiet hours are enforced 22:00-23:00.

name: Baguio Botanical Garden
fee_operational_notes: Standard adult fee; child discounts at gate.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Official Baguio VISITA page is JavaScript-rendered and unreadable by crawler; two secondary sources agree on 06:00-18:00 daily.

name: Baler Hanging Bridge
fee_operational_notes: Local structural preservation fee.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Free and ungated, and locals cross it as a daily commute, so it is never locked. It is closed in bad weather, and there is little shade.

name: Baler Lighthouse
fee_operational_notes: Local community checkpoint fee.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Out of service as a beacon. The climb is steep and the trail is slippery in the wet season, so the province discourages it then.

name: Banaue Rice Terraces
fee_operational_notes: Fee collected at the town center/triage area upon entry.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_source_label: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras
hours_note: The roadside viewpoint is free and ungated, but the terraces are worked farmland, not a park. Municipal tourism offices run 06:00-18:00, and the recommended hiking window is 06:00-17:00. A ₱50-100 environmental fee is collected at checkpoints.

name: Bangui Wind Farm
fee_operational_notes: Open public shoreline; no gate fees.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: The shoreline viewing area is free and ungated, so it is reachable at any hour; daylight is far better for viewing. The turbines themselves are an operating power facility and are closed to the public.

name: Bantay Abot Cave
fee_operational_notes: Free entry; optional ₱20 parking fee.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks
hours_note: A natural rock arch on the shore with no gate, ticket booth or posted hours, so it is reachable at any hour. Visit in daylight: the entrance is submerged at high tide.

name: Batad Rice Terraces
fee_operational_notes: Local community heritage checkpoint user fee.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_source_label: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras
hours_note: Unlike the Banaue viewpoint, Batad is a 45-minute hike down into the amphitheatre, so daylight governs: the recommended activity window is 06:00-17:00 and the trail gets dangerously slippery after rain. A guide is expected and a ₱100 heritage fee is collected at the Saddle.

name: BenCab Museum
fee_operational_notes: ₱200 for adults; ₱150 for students/seniors.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; museum/site admission

name: Burnham Park
fee_operational_notes: Free entry; boat rentals cost ₱100–₱150/hr.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: No gate and no closing time. The paid concessions (boat and bike rentals, skating) run roughly 07:00-18:00, and the Rose Garden and Orchidarium close around 18:00.

name: Caliraya Lake
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Public roads are free; resorts charge separate fees.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks; optional water/activity rental
hours_note: Viewing the lake from the Lumban–Caliraya–Cavinti road is free and ungated at any hour. The resorts along the shore set their own hours, typically 07:00-17:00 for day passes, and that is where the paid activities are.

name: Callao Cave
fee_operational_notes: Standard visitor entrance fee for cave path.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: A guide is mandatory and included in the fee. The Cagayan provincial government closed the cave temporarily in September 2025 for a safety review, so confirm it is open before travelling.

name: Calle Crisologo
fee_operational_notes: Public pedestrian heritage street; open 24/7.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: A public street in the Vigan heritage core, free and walkable at any hour. The shops and museums inside the ancestral houses keep their own hours, typically 09:00-18:00, and those are the ones that charge.

name: Camp John Hay
fee_operational_notes: ₱85 for Historical Core; eco-spaces are free.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: The grounds are a free public leisure zone, but every attraction inside has its own hours and fee: the Historical Core runs 09:00-17:00 and Tree Top Adventure roughly 09:00-18:00. Trails close in bad weather.

name: Cape Bojeador Lighthouse
fee_operational_notes: Local historical preservation donation.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Hours vary on holidays. The lighthouse still operates, so parts of the tower are closed to visitors.

name: Cape Engaño Lighthouse
fee_operational_notes: Covered within Palaui Island registration package.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Reachable only by a 45-minute to 3-hour guided trek across Palaui Island, or by boat to the cove and a 20-minute climb. No gate and no hours, but the trail is not marked, has no handrails, and is impassable in bad weather. The tower interior is restricted.

name: Chico River
fee_operational_notes: Free river access; rafting guides cost ₱1,500–₱2,500.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks; optional water/activity rental; activity/admission package
hours_note: The river is open year-round but white-water rafting is seasonal — the good water is July to January — and must be arranged in advance with a Kalinga operator, so there is no walk-up schedule. Runs take 3-4 hours, so morning starts are standard. The zigzag road through the park is light-vehicles only and dangerous.

name: Clark Freeport Zone
fee_operational_notes: Free zone entry; individual attractions vary.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: A 4,400-hectare economic zone rather than one attraction, entered free through guarded gates around the clock — you need valid ID to pass. Every attraction inside (Aqua Planet, the Clark Museum, Dinosaurs Island) keeps its own hours and fee.

name: Cloud 9 Antipolo
fee_operational_notes: Standard walk-in fee; fee is waived if dining at the restaurant.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: A private complex, so the 08:00-22:00 window is enforced rather than published by a city. The restaurant stops serving food around 21:00 and the view deck itself is the reason to come, so arrive well before closing.

name: Daranak Falls
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Standard adult general admission fee.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional water/activity rental
hours_note: Plastic and styrofoam are banned by municipal ordinance, as are alcohol and pets.

name: Dicasalarin Cove
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Day pass for private cove and weather station.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Privately owned by the Angara family, so it has a gate and a day-tour only window; sources range from 06:00-18:00 to 08:00-17:00, so 07:00-16:00 is the safe middle. Stay at Costa Pacifica for a discounted rate. The access road is narrow, steep and unlit.

name: Fort Santiago
fee_operational_notes: ₱150 for adults; ₱100 for students and seniors.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; museum/site admission
hours_note: Last entry 8:00 PM Mon-Fri, 8:30 PM Sat-Sun. Entry after that may be limited to advance bookings.

name: Hinulugang Taktak
fee_operational_notes: Base registration fee; pool usage runs extra.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Park hours are 07:00-16:00 but the activities run 08:00-15:00, so arrive early. Closed Mondays for maintenance; entry is currently free.

name: Hulugan Falls
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Trailhead fee; excludes optional guide tips.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional water/activity rental
hours_note: A registered guide is required. The last group is usually let start by 15:00 because guides must be back before dark, and the LGU closes the site entirely in heavy rain.

name: Hundred Islands National Park
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Environmental pass; excludes boat rentals.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional water/activity rental
hours_note: These are the Lucap Wharf visitor centre and boat-booking hours. The islets themselves are always accessible once you have a boat.

name: Ipo Dam View
fee_operational_notes: Free roadside viewing; watershed requires permit.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks
hours_note: The roadside view decks and the Mountain View park along the road are ungated and reachable at any hour for a ₱10-20 fee. Entering the dam itself is different: it is MWSS-operated, needs prior arrangement, security registration at several checkpoints, and a permit for groups of 30 or more.

name: Kapurpurawan Rock Formations
fee_operational_notes: Municipal fee to protect limestone rock faces.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: A natural site open in daylight hours; swimming and horse riding cost extra and have their own windows.

name: Kiltepan Viewpoint
fee_operational_notes: Local environment and cleanup fee at sunrise deck.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: An open mountainside with no gate, walked in the dark for sunrise — the trailhead is a 10-minute walk from town. It was closed after a 2018 fire and the main viewpoint has been closed or under repair at times since; Pog-o is the alternative. Expect crowds before 05:30.

name: La Mesa Eco Park
fee_operational_notes: Nature preserve maintenance and watershed fee.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Closed every Monday for maintenance, and a reservation is required — walk-ins are turned away because attendance is capped at 1,000 a day.

name: Las Casas Filipinas de Acuzar
fee_operational_notes: ₱2,500 standard pass; peak season pricing varies.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; activity/admission package
hours_source_label: Las Casas Filipinas de Acuzar official site
hours_note: A private heritage resort, so the day-tour window is enforced: guests may stay on the property 08:00-18:00. Walking tours run on fixed departure times, not open access, and an environmental fee is charged under a Bagac ordinance.

name: Masungi Georeserve
fee_operational_notes: ₱1,700 Weekday / ₱2,000 Weekend; requires booking.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; activity/admission package
hours_note: Visits must be booked ahead; trail start times vary by weekday vs weekend.

name: Mayon SkyDrive ATV Adventure
fee_operational_notes: Starts at ₱500; prices vary by trail length and vehicle size.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; activity/admission package
hours_note: A DOT-accredited operator, so the window is enforced, not published by a city. Rides start at 07:00 and the cut-off is 15:00 for long trails. Self-driving is 16+, the 4x4 and bike lanes have no comfort room on the trail, and operations stop in a typhoon or eruption.

name: Mayon Volcano Natural Park
fee_operational_notes: Mandatory environmental fees collected per person at designated park entry zones.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Always open as a protected area, but tourism activity is suspended or restricted by PHIVOLCS alert level, and the observation deck gets slippery in wet weather. The popular trailhead and viewing areas around Daraga, Tabaco and Malilipot are open 24/7; the paid Cagsawa Ruins park next to it is a separate 07:00-18:00 site.

name: Minalungao National Park
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Environmental river gorge registration fee.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional water/activity rental
hours_note: No swimming and no signal, and the water turns brown after a storm. Entrance has been quoted at ₱100 and ₱200 in different years, so check before going.

name: Minor Basilica of Our Lady of Piat
fee_operational_notes: Public pilgrimage site; free entry.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: The compound is open to visitors roughly 05:30-22:00; Masses run from 05:30 on Sundays and 06:00 on weekdays, latest ending 17:30. The parish office keeps separate weekday hours.

name: Mirador Heritage and Eco Park
fee_operational_notes: Upkeep fee for stone terrace trails and peace bell.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: One source lists 08:00-18:00 on weekdays and 07:30-19:00 at weekends, so 06:00-18:00 is the commonly cited daily window. No reservation needed except for events; pets and outside food are not allowed.

name: Mt. Batulao
fee_operational_notes: Cumulative registration across separate checkpoints.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: The main registration booth opens at 05:00, but the caretaker checkpoints further up the mountain are staffed around the clock, so pre-dawn starts are normal. A guide is now mandatory for every hiker, and weekend queues can stretch a 4-hour hike to 8.

name: Mt. Daraitan
fee_operational_notes: Unified environmental clearance and safety pass.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional camping/tent/campsite fee
hours_note: The registration desk opens at 03:00 and that is not a typo: the LGU caps the summit at 300 climbers a day, the cap fills before sunrise on weekends, and independent hiking is prohibited. Once full, late arrivals are redirected to the Tinipak River trek instead.

name: Mt. Pinatubo
fee_operational_notes: Includes domain tax, eco-clearance, and bot fees.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: This is the registration window at the Sta. Juliana tourism office, not a place you can walk into: you cannot hike independently, and a 4×4, guide and permit are mandatory. Registration closes at 07:00 sharp and the trail closes in the wet season.

name: Mt. Pulag
fee_operational_notes: DENR registration fee; excludes guide fees.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional camping/tent/campsite fee
hours_note: Ranger-station hours only. Access is DENR permit-controlled with daily quotas that sell out for the February–March sea-of-clouds season, so book weeks ahead. Trekkers typically start around 04:00 for sunrise.

name: Mt. Ulap
fee_operational_notes: Local registration fee per hiker at trailhead.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Registration at the Ampucao Barangay Hall opens 04:00 on weekends and 05:00 on weekdays; you cannot hike without a guide. The eco-trail was suspended and reopened on 16 September 2026 under EO 2026-71, so check for fresh advisories.

name: Museo De Baler
fee_operational_notes: Covers entry to historical exhibits to Doña Aurora Quezon House.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; museum/site admission
hours_note: Opened 30 June 2026 and free of charge; closed on government holidays.

name: Nagsasa Cove
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Base environmental user fee for coastal valley.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional water/activity rental; optional camping/tent/campsite fee
hours_note: A natural cove with no gate, so the beach itself has no hours; the constraint is the banca from Pundaquit, which only runs in daylight. Facilities are basic: no electricity or mobile signal.

name: National Museum of the Philippines
fee_operational_notes: Free entry for visitors; groups of 20+ must book online in advance.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; museum/site admission
hours_note: All regional branches keep the same 09:00-18:00 window; open every day.

name: Palaui Island
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Separate mandatory guide and boat rental rates apply.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional camping/tent/campsite fee
hours_note: An uninhabited protected island with no facilities, reached only by chartered banca from San Vicente port. There are no posted hours, but boats are weather-bound: July to October crossings are frequently cancelled, and there is no phone signal on the island.

name: Paoay Sand Dunes Adventures
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Fits 5 people per 4x4; package includes unlimited sandboarding.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; activity/admission package
hours_note: Driver-reported start times run earlier than these posted hours, so book the ride before travelling.

name: Pintô Art Museum
fee_operational_notes: ₱250 for adults; ₱200 for seniors/students.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; museum/site admission

name: Quezon Protected Landscape
fee_operational_notes: Separate vehicle environmental fees and trail guide costs apply.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional camping/tent/campsite fee
hours_note: A free protected area with no gate, open around the clock; the facilities inside it are what close, with the Zigzag Park stores shutting around 18:00-19:00. Quezon Adventure Park and the Herbal Pavilion are undergoing a ₱10M rehabilitation, so parts may be restricted.

name: Rizal Park
fee_operational_notes: Free public park; enclosed gardens cost ₱10–₱20.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks

name: Sabang Beach
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Open public municipal surf break; no gates.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks; optional water/activity rental
hours_note: A public beach with no entrance fee and no gate. Surf lessons and board rental are what cost money, and the surf season runs September to February.

name: Sagada
fee_operational_notes: Mandatory tourist tracking card fee at tourism center.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: A scattered mountain municipality rather than one gated site, so there is no single set of hours. The tourism office itself is open 08:00-17:00 daily, and every cave and Echo Valley route needs a registered guide plus a ₱50 registration fee.

name: Sagada Sumaguing Cave
fee_operational_notes: Covers 4 guests; requires separate town environmental receipt.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: A registered guide is mandatory and must be booked in person. The Sagada LGU closes the cave periodically, so confirm the day you travel.

name: San Agustin Church of Paoay
fee_operational_notes: National historical landmark; free entry.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: Posted visiting hours are 08:00-11:55 and 13:30-17:00 because of services; the exterior is visible at any time. Interior access varies by day.

name: San Juan La Union
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Mandatory eco-tourism environmental fee collected from tourists.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional water/activity rental
hours_note: Urbiztondo Beach has no gate and no posted hours. The LGU collects a ₱50 environmental fee per person, and surf schools run lessons roughly 06:00-17:00.

name: Seven Lakes of San Pablo
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Free public lake lines; tricycle loops vary in cost.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks
hours_note: Seven separate crater lakes, not one site, and each is run by its own community. The Sampaloc promenade beside City Hall is free and ungated; Pandin runs paid 2-hour bamboo-raft tours from roughly 07:00 to 17:00. Fees are set per lake and change, so verify with the city tourism office.

name: Sierra Madre Mountain View
fee_operational_notes: Open highway overlooks; roadside cafe orders separate.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks
hours_note: A dispersed mountain range rather than one gated viewpoint, so no single set of hours applies; the ridgelines and river areas around Tanay are reached on foot from several barangays.

name: Taal Basilica
fee_operational_notes: Free entry; ₱50 fee applies to climb bell tower.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: Gate hours are wider than the Mass schedule; church events can close it.

name: Taal Heritage Town
fee_operational_notes: Free public street access; home donations vary.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: Individual ancestral houses and museums inside the heritage district keep their own hours, often shorter than the district window.

name: Taal Volcano View
fee_operational_notes: Commercial parks or restaurants charge separate entry fees.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks
hours_note: This is the Tagaytay ridge view, which is free from the roadside at any hour. It is NOT the crater: landing on Volcano Island follows the PHIVOLCS alert level and is typically closed at level 2 or above, and it has been at level 1 for extended periods. The paid ridge viewpoints keep their own hours.

name: Tagaytay Picnic Grove
fee_operational_notes: Standard adult entry token for eco-ridge trails.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee
hours_note: Some sources list 08:00-20:00 with later weekend starts, so treat 06:00-22:00 as the outer window and confirm before relying on the edges. Arrive early: afternoon cloud usually hides the volcano.

name: Tinipak River and Rock Formation
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Combined barangay environment and rock formation pass.
possible_expenses: local transfer/boat share or local ride; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; optional water/activity rental; optional camping/tent/campsite fee
hours_note: A guide is mandatory and registration is on-site only, with no online booking and no card payment — bring cash. The river can flash-flood with little warning, and swimming is limited to marked zones because of sinkholes.

name: Vigan Heritage Site
fee_operational_notes: Free historical public district block access.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: The inscribed historic town is a living district with no gate, so it is accessible at any hour. Individual museums and ancestral homes charge small fees and keep separate hours.

name: Wright Park
fee_operational_notes: Free park lanes; horseback loops cost ₱200–₱300/hr.
possible_expenses: local transport; food/drinks
hours_note: Ungated and free, so walkable at any hour. Horseback riding, the only paid activity, runs from about 07:00 until sunset.

name: Zoobic Safari
activities: Variable — no standalone current rate verified
fee_operational_notes: Matches the standard Subic Freeport ticket gate rate.
possible_expenses: local ride to jump-off; guide/registration where required; food/drinks; entrance/environmental fee; activity/admission package
hours_note: Last admission 14:00. Sources disagree on the closing time (16:00 vs 18:00) and the park closes on most public holidays, so confirm on the day.
